At a red light stop before the stop line or the crosswalk, whichever comes first, and wait for green, although a green arrow that comes on during the red allows travel in the arrow's direction.

A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red, and a driver who is too close to the intersection to stop safely should proceed through with caution.

A flashing circular red light is treated exactly like a stop sign: come to a stop, give way to every pedestrian, bicyclist and vehicle, and then go.

A flashing yellow light means slow down, scan the intersection, yield to any oncoming vehicles before attempting a left turn, and proceed with caution.

title.text: Move over and yield for emergency

why_how.text: When a vehicle with flashing blue or red lights or a sounding siren approaches from any direction, the law requires you to pull over to the right side of the road, stop, and stay stopped until the emergency or law enforcement vehicle has passed.
An approaching emergency vehicle requires you to pull right and stop until it passes, while a stopped one requires caution, slowing and where possible a lane change rather than a stop.

When you come upon a stopped police car showing flashing blue lights or a stopped emergency vehicle showing flashing red lights you must slow down and proceed with caution, and on a four lane road like an interstate you must also move over a lane whenever that can be done safely.
A stopped emergency vehicle calls for slowing down everywhere, but the additional duty to change lanes applies only on a four lane highway and only when the change is safe.

A maintenance vehicle of the state, a city or a town that is working on a highway has the right-of-way, so a driver coming up on a snowplow with its lights flashing must slow with caution and give way to it.
Towing and repair vehicles usually show amber flashing lights, and a driver must use the same caution and procedures around these stopped vehicles as around stopped police and emergency vehicles.

During a police stop keep your safety belt fastened until the officer has seen you wearing it, limit your own movements and those of passengers, breathe deeply and stay calm while the officer explains the reason for the stop.

When the officer asks, show your license, vehicle registration and proof of insurance, stay in the vehicle unless asked to get out, and in a dimly lit area turn on the interior lights after stopping and before the officer approaches.
The roadside is not the place to argue a traffic offense; the time to address it is in court.
A police officer may direct you through a red light, and you should follow the officer's directions with caution.

title.text: Stop, yield and railroad sign shapes

why_how.text: A road sign's meaning can be told from its shape and color as well as its wording, so a sign covered by dirt or snow can still be read as regulatory, warning or information from its shape alone.

A stop sign has eight sides; at it you come to a full stop ahead of the stop line, the marked or unmarked crosswalk or the cross road, whichever is reached first, then scan the intersection, give way as required and proceed.
A yield right-of-way sign is shaped like an upside down triangle and means slow down, search, and enter only when the way is clear of pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles.
A circular sign bearing a large X and the letters RR warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.
